concepts.def: Regular tightly-packed particles vibrating in fixed positions.
Particles close together but able to flow past each other.
Particles far apart, moving fast and randomly in all directions.
Solid → liquid at the melting point; energy breaks regular structure.

(s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) aqueous (dissolved in water).

walkthroughs.body_html:
States of Matter — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

States of Matter brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with States of Matter.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which state symbol means dissolved in water?
options: (aq)
are fixed in place
touch but slide
are far apart and move fast
have no energy

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.

mcqs.q: For a process to be spontaneous, what must happen to the total entropy of the universe?
options: The entropy of the system must increase for the process to be spontaneous.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
It must increase (ΔS_total > 0) — the system's entropy alone can decrease as long as the surroundings' entropy increases more.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The entropy of the surroundings must stay constant for the process to be spontaneous.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
